title: Nippaug (Little Fresh Pond)
summary: Nippaug is a later suggested Algonquian-style name for Little Fresh Pond, kept here with caution because the naming history differs from older local placename records.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Little Fresh Pond / North Sea location from public map/search context; not exact historic coordinate
introduction_content: Nippaug is listed as a name suggested for Little Fresh Pond between Southampton village and North Sea. The name shows how some Long Island place-name forms were created or applied in later local history writing.
history_content: Nippaug is a later suggested name rather than a deeply attested early place name. The name preserves the modern pond association and the caution around its source history.
translation_content:
The name is explained as water-land or water-place, from language connected with water and land or place. Tooker compares Nippaug with Nappeag and points readers to Napock for related water-place vocabulary.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are integral to the symbols representing what's on the ground, giving context to space, helping us navigate from one place to another, enabling informative communication, linking the stories behind them, providing identity and asserting rights.”

— Wendy Shaw, Place names and people (2016), conference abstract
whereintheworld_content: Map location note: The pin is placed near Little Fresh Pond in North Sea, Southampton, using a modern pond-area point. It is not an exact historic coordinate or evidence of an early recorded placename.
